turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (NURSE): Right, come on through. Before the doctor sees you I'll do the temperature. You were saying it was up at home?
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): Yeah, this morning the little thermometer said 37.8. I was after a hot cup of tea, mind you. And the parking out there is a disgrace, we went round three times.
[SEG0003] person_1 (NURSE): Mm. I've got 36.9 now, oxygen 98 percent, pulse 78. You're grand. He'll be along in a minute.
[SEG0004] person_2 (PATIENT): 36.9, sure that's nothing.
[SEG0005] person_3 (DOCTOR): Hello there, I'm Dr Brennan. What's brought you in?
[SEG0006] person_2 (PATIENT): The nose, doctor. Blocked solid, a pressure across the face, and green stuff coming out of it. I'm after a cold.
[SEG0007] person_4 (CAREGIVER): She's been bad the bones of two weeks, green the whole time, she's wrecked tired, and she sleeps terribly. I'm with her in the house so I hear her up.
[SEG0008] person_2 (PATIENT): Ah now. The cold was about a fortnight ago. The green and the blocked nose and the pressure, that's ten days. And I do not sleep terribly.

[SEG0009] person_3 (DOCTOR): So the cold was about two weeks back, then ten days of blockage, facial pressure and green discharge, and you're tired. On the sleep, you and your carer don't quite agree, so I'll note that.
[SEG0010] person_2 (PATIENT): Yeah, err, the tiredness is into the second week. I'm flat, but I still did the messages yesterday. The dog next door barked half the night, that's a whole other saga.
[SEG0011] person_3 (DOCTOR): Any fever today, toothache, or a proper headache?
[SEG0012] person_2 (PATIENT): No fever. No toothache. It's pressure, not a headache, over the cheeks and the forehead.
[SEG0013] person_4 (CAREGIVER): And she skips the tablets on Sundays. The loratadine. That cut on her finger healed in five days, healed perfect, not a bother.
[SEG0014] person_2 (PATIENT): Saturdays, not Sundays. The hurling is on and I forget the tablet. The cut was a nick off a tin opener, nothing to it.
[SEG0015] person_3 (DOCTOR): The loratadine, what dose is it, and what are you taking it for?
[SEG0016] person_2 (PATIENT): The ten mg one, once a day, for the hay fever. Except Saturdays, like I said. Umm, I stopped the cetirizine in March, it had me dozy on the tills.
[SEG0017] person_3 (DOCTOR): Are you using anything in the nose?

[SEG0018] person_2 (PATIENT): Otrivine, two sprays each side, morning and night, every day since this started. There was talk of a steroid one, beclamethasone or whatever you call it. I never got that from the chemist.
[SEG0019] person_4 (CAREGIVER): My own sister is on a steroid spray for years for her sinuses. Swears by it. Different nose to this one, mind.
[SEG0020] person_1 (NURSE): My little fella had an awful cold last month. Three days off school and then he was flying. I'll leave ye to it.
[SEG0021] person_3 (DOCTOR): Any allergy to medicines, penicillin, anything at all?
[SEG0022] person_2 (PATIENT): No. Nothing like that. I was put on amoxicillin last spring for a chest thing and I stopped it in March, the tummy was at me. Didn't finish the box.
[SEG0023] person_3 (DOCTOR): Right, so that was stopped, and it wasn't an allergy. How about the chest now, the breathing, any trouble?
[SEG0024] person_2 (PATIENT): Chest is grand. No cough really left.
[SEG0025] person_3 (DOCTOR): Any swelling round the eyes, or trouble with the vision?
[SEG0026] person_2 (PATIENT): No. Eyes are fine.
[SEG0027] person_3 (DOCTOR): Let me see. The nose is congested both sides, there's a bit of green mucus, no swelling of the face, and the throat is clear.

[SEG0028] person_3 (DOCTOR): The little drainage holes from the sinuses swell up after a cold, so the mucus sits there and the pressure builds. The green is just your body clearing it. That on its own doesn't mean a germ that needs an antibiotic.
[SEG0029] person_2 (PATIENT): So not straight onto an antibiotic? My cousin was on them for weeks, but sure that's her own business.

[SEG0030] person_3 (DOCTOR): Most of these settle without antibiotics. Stop the Otrivine, you've been on it long enough and it can make the blockage bounce back. Salt water rinses, and paracetamol for the pressure if you need it.
[SEG0031] person_2 (PATIENT): Paracetamol I take the odd time, two of the 500s, not every day. Grand.

[SEG0032] person_3 (DOCTOR): I'll leave a back-up script for amoxicillin, 500 milligrams three times a day for five days. Only start it if the blockage, the pressure and the green discharge are still there in three days. Take it with food, given the tummy the last time.
[SEG0033] person_4 (CAREGIVER): And if she's worse before that, what then?

[SEG0034] person_3 (DOCTOR): Come back if she's not better in a week, or sooner if there's a fever, swelling round the eye, or the pain gets severe. Keep the hay fever tablet daily, Saturdays as well if you can.
[SEG0035] person_2 (PATIENT): Right so. I'll try the rinses. Coming back, the parking will be worse than the nose, I'm telling you.
[SEG0036] person_3 (DOCTOR): We'll see you if you need us. Mind yourselves.

spec.situation: Blocked nose, facial pressure and green discharge ten days after a cold; second week of tiredness; uses nasal spray daily; doctor explains most settle without antibiotics, gives a back-up plan.

traps.happens: A caregiver or relative reports observations ('the cut healed in five days', 'she sleeps badly', 'he does not take the tablets on Sundays'); the patient agrees, disagrees or corrects one point. The nurse also reports a measurement that the patient mentioned before.
traps.label_rule: reported_by follows who said it. A healing cut that healed normally is a negative finding (no slow-healing wounds) or nothing, NOT a symptom. A disputed fact is recorded with certainty disputed or as an uncertainty. A correction replaces the earlier value (Saturday, not Sunday).

traps.happens: The doctor (or nurse) explains a mechanism or a diagnosis in the patient's body ('the voice box is irritated by reflux', 'diabetes dulls the nerves in the feet', 'the swelling is your body fighting infection'). A nurse or caregiver also mentions a fact about THEIR OWN life (their sister, their child, their own illness).
traps.label_rule: Explanations by the doctor are NEVER symptoms, history or social history of the patient; they may only appear as clinical_assessment or counselling if the doctor stated them as such. A nurse's or caregiver's own life facts are not recorded as the patient's. Each symptom's reported_by is the person who really described it.

features: stopped_or_never_taken: a medicine the patient stopped, was never given or only took once ('I stopped it in March'). Status discontinued, not current; a medicine never taken is not recorded as a medication.
relative_speaks_for_patient: a relative answers for the patient and the patient partly contradicts; reported_by follows who said it.
